interpretations: Patients qualify if at least one of their laboratory records has U-PRO = '-' and at least one (possibly a different) record has RA = '-'. All of the patient's lab records are then used for the averages.
Patients qualify only if a single laboratory record has both U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-'. All of the patient's lab records are then used for the averages.
Patients qualify under interpretation 1 or 2, but only the records with U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-' are used for the averages, rather than all of the patient's records.
The per-patient average of TAT − TAT2 is the average of (TAT − TAT2) computed row by row. Rows where either TAT or TAT2 is null are ignored.
The per-patient average of TAT − TAT2 is AVG(TAT) − AVG(TAT2), with each average ignoring nulls independently. The two columns may then be averaged over different sets of rows.
The final PT value is the unweighted mean of the per-patient PT averages, so each patient counts equally. This is the literal reading.
The final PT value is the mean over all records of the qualifying patients, so patients with more records weigh more.
A patient with no non-null PT in any record has no PT average and is excluded from the PT mean. The same patient can still contribute to the TAT − TAT2 mean.
A patient with no non-null PT is excluded from both final values, so both means use the same set of patients.
"Exactly '-'" means an exact string match, so values such as '+-', '- ', or null do not count.
"Exactly '-'" means a case-insensitive or whitespace-trimmed match to '-'.
The question could be read as asking for two separate result columns, the average PT and the average TAT − TAT2, in a single row. This is the stated output.
The question could be read as asking for the average difference between the per-patient PT average and the per-patient TAT − TAT2 average. This is less likely.
A patient's PT average is taken over the PT column of Laboratory only. Examination and Patient tables are not involved, although the patient could be required to exist in the Patient table.
Patients are identified by Laboratory.ID. Any lab record whose ID has no matching Patient row is still included.
Patients are identified by Laboratory.ID. Only patients who also exist in the Patient table are included.
Missing interpretations:

Patients qualify if the U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-' conditions are checked against different tables or dates (for example, the patient's latest lab record only), so only the most recent record decides qualification.
The per-patient TAT − TAT2 average is computed only over rows where PT is also non-null, so every statistic uses the same set of rows.
A patient whose TAT − TAT2 average is undefined (all TAT or TAT2 null) is excluded from the TAT − TAT2 mean only. It can still contribute to the PT mean.
A patient with an undefined PT average or an undefined TAT − TAT2 average is excluded from both final values, so both means use only patients with both averages defined.
A patient with an undefined per-patient average is treated as 0 instead of being ignored.
